subject: Approval needed: Early-exit & ramp schedule for Horizon Health - downsell protections
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Deal Desk <dealdesk@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 8 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Early-exit amendment + ramp schedule for Horizon Health (requires exec ok)

Team,

Horizon Health (Horizon) is pushing for an amendment to their SOW to add a customer-friendly early-exit option and a 6-month ramp schedule tied to seat to usage reductions. They want:

- An opt-out clause allowing termination after month 3 with 60 days notice and a pro-rated refund for unused prepaid months.
- A ramp schedule that guarantees baseline committed spend for the first 6 months, then a step-down option reducing commitments by up to 40% if usage drops.
- Request for a 20% initial discount during the ramp months.

They flagged two concerns: downsell protection (so we don't lose all revenue immediately) and language that prevents gaming the ramp. Legal flagged non-standard terms. Finance is worried about the revenue hit if we allow the 40% step down immediately.

Attaching their draft amendment and our initial redlines. Need exec approval for:
- Whether we accept the 60-day opt-out with pro-rated refunds and no termination fee;
- Maximum allowed step-down percentage and minimum guarantee length;
- Whether a 20% ramp discount is acceptable or needs to be lower.

Proposed guardrails from sales: 3-month minimum commitment before opt-out; 6-month ramp but max 25% allowed step-down in any single quarter; discount capped at 15%. I recommend we escalate to Marissa and Finance (Vivek) + Legal (Aditya) for formal sign-off.

Attachments: Horizon_HS_Amendment_v2.docx, redlines_Horizon_Amendment.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Early-exit amendment + ramp schedule for Horizon Health (requires exec ok)

Karthik — thanks for the write-up and attachments. This is the kind of ask that should have clear measurable guardrails. My initial thoughts:

- Opt-out: We should not agree to a pure pro-rated refund without some termination fee or minimum commitment. Recommend: opt-out allowed after month 3 with a 30% termination fee of remaining committed value OR pro-rata refund minus a 10% operational recovery fee.
- Ramp schedule: 6 months is acceptable, but step-downs should be phased. Proposal: maximum 15% reduction at the 3-month mark and additional 10% at month 6 (cumulative max 25%). This prevents an immediate 40% drop.
- Discount: 15% cap during ramp is reasonable. Anything above 15% needs SVP approval.

Vivek — finance input on the termination fee vs refund math is needed. Aditya — please draft compliant language that addresses "no gaming" (e.g., usage measurement, minimum trailing 30-day average, and lock-out on immediate recontracting for reduced seats).

If legal and finance sign off, I can approve up to 15% discount for the ramp period. Anything beyond that I will escalate to the CRO.

-Marissa
VP Sales | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Mar 2026 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Early-exit amendment + ramp schedule for Horizon Health (requires exec ok)

Marissa / Karthik — I reviewed the draft amendment and inserted redlines. Summary of legal position and suggested language (high level):

1) Early Termination / Refunds: We can offer a pro-rated refund but only after deducting a termination charge equal to 25% of the outstanding committed value OR, alternatively, allow termination with a 60-day notice and no refund but with a termination fee equal to one month of committed services (whichever is higher). This preserves a recovery path.

2) Ramp & Downsell Protections: Define a "ramp schedule" as an explicit schedule in Exhibit A. Include a clause preventing immediate churn-based recontracting: any decreases greater than 15% in committed units will be applied prospectively and subject to a 90-day measurement window. Also require that any step-down be reflected in a signed change order.

3) Discounting: Limit cumulative discounts during ramp to 15%. Approvals beyond that require documented CRO approval.

4) Measurement & Anti-gaming: Use rolling 30-day average for usage thresholds. Add audit rights if Horizon contests measurements.

I attached a redlined PDF (redlines_Horizon_Amendment.pdf) showing exact language. If Finance prefers, we can convert the termination fee into an earn-out tied to actual usage over the next 3 months (contact Vivek for modeling).

For approval flow: Legal signs off on the language; Finance confirms revenue impact; Marissa (VP Sales) can sign up to 15% discount. Anything beyond goes to the CRO.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Commercial Transactions | Redwood Inference

Karthik — appreciate the quick turnaround and the conversation today. We can accept the proposed phased step-down (15% at 3 months, additional 10% at 6 months) and the 15% capped ramp discount, provided the opt-out path is workable for our finance team.

For clarity: we prefer the opt-out with a pro-rated refund after month 3 and a 60-day notice; the termination charge is acceptable if it is framed as an administrative recovery (Horizon prefers a fixed one-month fee rather than a percentage, but can accept 25% if needed).

Please send the final redline and DocuSign envelope when you have approval.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
VP, Procurement | Horizon Health
